outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no result has been found that settles or moves the L_{ω1,ω} categoricity bullet as worded. The only in-window items are a 2024 journal publication (JEMS) of a 2018 preprint about AECs, and an October 2024 preprint titled 'Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities' that concerns a different Shelah conjecture (local Hanf number below 2^ℵ0). The one claim that reaches the L_{ω1,ω} case, Espíndola's 2019 ZFC proof, is unrefereed as far as found (latest arXiv version April 2022, no journal reference) and does not state the bullet's threshold as a separate theorem.
problem_asks: Read from the frozen bullet alone (pipeline wording: 'Shelah's categoricity conjecture for L_{ω1,ω}: If a sentence is categorical above the Hanf number then it is categorical in all cardinals above the Hanf number'). (1) Scope: sentences of the logic L_{ω1,ω}. The bullet does not state whether the vocabulary is countable; the standard published form (Boney–Vasey 2015; nLab) takes a countable language, and the bullet is silent. (2) Hypothesis: the sentence is categorical above the Hanf number. The wording does not say whether this means categorical in SOME cardinal above the Hanf number (the usual Shelah form, cited as: categorical in some λ ≥ threshold) or in ALL cardinals above it (which would make the implication trivial). Both readings are recorded here; the sources use the first. (3) Threshold: 'the Hanf number' of the logic. The bullet gives no numerical value. Sources cited in the literature use ℶ_{ω1} (Shelah 1983 Conjecture 2, as cited by Boney–Vasey 2015 and nLab); one search-summary source gives i_{ω1}; Espíndola 2019 leaves the threshold as 'the maximum of the Hanf numbers for categoricity and non-categoricity'. (4) Conclusion: the sentence is categorical in every cardinal λ at or above that threshold. A resolution of the whole bullet needs (1) through (4) all covered; a result restricted to universal sentences, to a higher or different threshold, to AECs, or to a different logic leaves parts open.

events.what_happened: UNVERIFIED, secondary only: Keisler is credited with a Morley-type categoricity theorem for L_{ω1,ω} that assumes in addition that the model in the categoricity cardinal is sequentially homogeneous; Shelah later showed, using an example of Marcus, that this assumption does not follow from categoricity. Cited in search summaries of arXiv 1506.07024 and nLab; the primary Keisler paper was not located or opened, and 1506.07024's abstract does not mention Keisler (checked when opened).
events.delivers: Under an extra hypothesis (sequential homogeneity of the model at the categoricity cardinal), a Morley-style transfer for L_{ω1,ω}. Restriction: the extra hypothesis, which the conjecture does not assume.
events.remains: The unconditional conjecture: categoricity in some cardinal at or above the threshold, without sequential homogeneity, implying categoricity in all cardinals above it.
events.doubts: Source not opened; the claim rests on search-summary text only. The sequential homogeneity assumption is the reason it is a partial result under a different hypothesis.
events.direction: Partial, consistent with the conjecture; proves a version with an added hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Hart and Shelah, 'Categoricity over P for first order T or categoricity for φ in L_{ω1,ω} can stop at ℵ_k while holding for ℵ_0,...,ℵ_{k-1}' (Shelah [HaSh:323]), Israel J. Math. 70 (1990) 219–235. For each k they give an L_{ω1,ω} sentence φ_k that is ℵ_n-categorical for n<k but not beth_k-categorical (the abstract says beth_k, not ℵ_k).
events.revisions: arXiv math/9201240 v1; the fetched arXiv page gives submission date 15 January 1990, though the ID's '9201' suggests a 1992 posting. Journal 1990 (Israel J. Math. 70).
events.delivers: Examples showing that categoricity at ℵ_0..ℵ_{k-1} for an L_{ω1,ω} sentence does not propagate to beth_k. Restriction: the examples are at cardinals below the threshold; they do not test categoricity in cardinals at or above the Hanf number.
events.remains: All of the conjecture: the examples are at small cardinals and say nothing about categoricity above the threshold.
events.direction: Neighbouring: shows categoricity below the threshold can fail to continue. Does not bear on the threshold statement itself.
events.object: φ_k, an L_{ω1,ω} sentence with a relative first-order theory T_k, built explicitly to be ℵ_n-categorical for n<k and not beth_k-categorical. Construction details were not read; the abstract describes it only.

events.what_happened: UNVERIFIED, secondary only: Makkai and Shelah, 'Categoricity of theories in L_{κω}, with κ a compact cardinal', Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 47 (1990) 41–97. Cited in a search summary as proving Shelah's categoricity conjecture for L_{κ,ω} when κ is strongly compact. Not opened: Boney's 1303.0550 does not mention it (checked), and the primary paper was not located.
events.delivers: Per the secondary summary: categoricity transfer for L_{κ,ω} with κ strongly compact. Restriction: a different logic (L_{κ,ω}, not L_{ω1,ω}) and a large-cardinal hypothesis.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} case, which has no large-cardinal hypothesis in the bullet.
events.doubts: Unverified. The claim is a secondary summary; the citation details are as given there.
events.direction: Analogue: a different logic and a large-cardinal hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Kolman and Shelah, 'Categoricity and amalgamation for AEC and κ measurable' (Sh:362), arXiv math/9602216, v1 submitted 15 February 1996, Fund. Math. 151 (1996) 209–240. For a theory T in L_{κ,ℵ0} with κ measurable that is categorical in some λ > κ, the models of T of cardinality in [|T|+κ, λ) have the amalgamation property.
events.revisions: v1 15 Feb 1996; a later revised arXiv version recasts the result for AECs (per the fetched page).
events.delivers: Amalgamation for lower-cardinality models of a categorical L_{κ,ℵ0}-theory under a measurable-cardinal hypothesis. Restriction: the logic is L_{κ,ℵ0} with κ measurable, not L_{ω1,ω} without a large-cardinal assumption.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} categoricity transfer above the threshold.
events.direction: Analogue: amalgamation rather than a categoricity transfer, in a different logic, under a large-cardinal hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Categoricity of abstract classes with amalgamation' (Sh:394), arXiv math/9809197, submitted 15 September 1998, Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 98 (1999) 261–294. For an abstract elementary class K with amalgamation and a suitable Hanf number χ_0: if χ_0 < λ_0 ≤ λ_1 and K is categorical in λ_1^+, then K is categorical in λ_0.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 only, per the fetched page.
events.delivers: Downward categoricity transfer for AECs with amalgamation. Restriction: AECs with amalgamation, not L_{ω1,ω} sentences; the abstract does not mention a successor hypothesis for the result it gives.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} conjecture. The result is about downward transfer among cardinals above χ_0 for AECs with amalgamation, which the L_{ω1,ω} sentences of the bullet do not have in general.

events.what_happened: Vasey, 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in universal classes: part I', arXiv 1506.07024 v1 submitted 23 June 2015 (revised to v11, 5 March 2017), Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 168 (2017) 1609–1642. For a universal class categorical in cardinals of arbitrarily high cofinality, categoricity on a tail of cardinals, in ZFC without assuming a successor categoricity cardinal; for AECs with amalgamation under tameness, shortness and prime-model assumptions, categoricity in some λ > H_2 implies categoricity in all λ' ≥ H_2 with H_2 an explicit Hanf-type bound.
events.revisions: v1 23 Jun 2015; v11 5 Mar 2017 (journal version APAL 2017).
events.delivers: Categoricity transfer for universal classes (cofinality hypothesis) and, under tameness and shortness, for AECs with amalgamation with an explicit bound H_2. Restriction: universal classes or tame AECs with amalgamation; the page does not mention L_{ω1,ω}.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} conjecture as worded: no sentence-level statement for L_{ω1,ω} and no threshold equal to ℶ_{ω1}.

checked_by.who: Annals of Pure and Applied Logic (journal of record)

events.direction: Analogue: categoricity transfer for universal classes and tame AECs, consistent with the conjecture's shape but not its statement.

events.what_happened: Boney and Vasey, 'Categoricity and infinitary logics', arXiv 1508.03316 v1 submitted 13 August 2015, v2 revised 16 October 2015 (comment: 'major changes after a mistake was discovered in the previous version'). Identifies a gap in Shelah's proof of a claim about AECs categorical in unboundedly many cardinals (the claim: for large M, N in K, M ≤ N iff M ⪯ N in L_{∞,LS(K)^+}). Assuming the corrected claim, the set of cardinals where K is categorical, has amalgamation and a good λ-frame is stationary. The paper also states the L_{ω1,ω} categoricity conjecture as open.
events.delivers: A stationarity result for categoricity cardinals of AECs, conditional on the claim. Restriction: AECs with amalgamation and a good frame; it does not settle a categoricity transfer for L_{ω1,ω}.
events.remains: The whole L_{ω1,ω} conjecture; the paper is a correction of Shelah's AEC proof and does not treat L_{ω1,ω} sentences above the threshold.
events.doubts: The paper itself reports that Shelah's proof of the claim had a gap, and that the stationarity theorem is conditional on the claim. A search summary also says an earlier attempt to repair the gap was itself found to be wrong; that remark was not verified in the paper's text.
events.direction: Neighbouring: AEC stationarity under a conditional claim. Does not bear on the threshold statement.

events.what_happened: Vasey, 'Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture in universal classes. Part II', arXiv 1602.02633 v1 submitted 8 February 2016 (v3 26 Oct 2016), Selecta Mathematica 23 (2017) 1469–1506. Main theorem: for a universal L_{ω1,ω} sentence ψ, if ψ is categorical in some λ ≥ ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}, then ψ is categorical in all λ' ≥ ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}. Works in ZFC, no successor assumption, no amalgamation assumption, no large cardinals; extends to uncountable languages; a corollary gives amalgamation above the threshold.
events.revisions: v1 8 Feb 2016; v2 6 Sep 2016; v3 26 Oct 2016; journal Selecta 2017.
events.delivers: For UNIVERSAL L_{ω1,ω} sentences only, categoricity in some λ ≥ ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}} implies categoricity in all λ' ≥ ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}, in ZFC. Restriction 1: universal sentences, not all L_{ω1,ω} sentences. Restriction 2: threshold ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}, a larger bound than ℶ_{ω1}, so it does not give the bullet's threshold.
events.remains: Non-universal L_{ω1,ω} sentences, and the threshold ℶ_{ω1} (if that is the intended Hanf number). The result is a partial result on the bullet's statement, not the statement.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture (categoricity transfer), on a restricted class of sentences and with a larger threshold.

events.what_happened: Vasey, 'On categoricity in successive cardinals', arXiv 1810.10061 v1 submitted 23 October 2018 (v4 19 Mar 2020). For a universal L_{ω1,ω} sentence categorical on an end segment of cardinals below β_ω (= ℶ_ω), it is categorical everywhere above ℶ_ω; in ZFC, without amalgamation or arbitrarily large models; extends to tame AECs with weak amalgamation. Journal: DOI 10.1017/jsl.2020.25 (Journal of Symbolic Logic). A search summary gives 2022 for the journal; the DOI suggests 2020; not resolved.
events.delivers: For universal L_{ω1,ω} sentences: categoricity on an end segment of cardinals below ℶ_ω implies categoricity above ℶ_ω. Restrictions: universal sentences; the hypothesis is categoricity on a whole end segment below ℶ_ω (many cardinals), not categoricity in one cardinal at or above ℶ_{ω1}; threshold ℶ_ω.
events.remains: Non-universal sentences; the hypothesis form of the bullet (one categoricity cardinal above the Hanf number); the threshold ℶ_{ω1}.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper; publication year not resolved (2020 per DOI, 2022 per a search summary)

events.direction: Partial, consistent with the conjecture; universal sentences and a different hypothesis form.

events.what_happened: Vasey, 'The categoricity spectrum of large abstract elementary classes', arXiv 1805.04068 v1 submitted 10 May 2018, latest v7 2 Oct 2019. Classifies possible categoricity spectra of AECs with amalgamation and arbitrarily large models (assuming injective cardinal exponentiation): empty, an end segment starting below the Hanf number, or a closed interval; a second result for AECs with no maximal models under a strengthening of GCH. Journal reference not found in the fetched page.
events.delivers: A classification of categoricity spectra for AECs with amalgamation and arbitrarily large models, under injective exponentiation. Restriction: AECs, not L_{ω1,ω} sentences; injective exponentiation and amalgamation.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} conjecture; the classification concerns AECs and does not establish the threshold for sentences.
events.direction: Analogue for AECs, relevant to the Hanf-number threshold in the AEC setting.

events.what_happened: Shelah and Vasey, 'Categoricity and multidimensional diagrams', arXiv 1805.06291 v1 submitted 16 May 2018 (v5 9 Mar 2023). Proves the eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs assuming a proper class of strongly compact cardinals, and for AECs with amalgamation under a weak version of GCH. Published in J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), no. 7, 2301–2372. The publication year (2024) is inside the window; the first written argument is the 2018 preprint.
events.revisions: v1 16 May 2018; v5 9 Mar 2023; journal JEMS 2024.
events.delivers: Eventual categoricity for AECs under a proper class of strongly compact cardinals; for AECs with amalgamation under weak GCH. Restriction: AECs; the page states no results on L_{ω1,ω} sentences and no threshold equal to ℶ_{ω1}.
events.remains: The L_{ω1,ω} conjecture as worded: the paper's results are for AECs, and whether L_{ω1,ω} classes are covered as a special case is not stated on the abstract page; the threshold is not stated.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (journal of record)

events.doubts: Hypotheses: a large cardinal (strongly compact) for the general result; weak GCH for the amalgamation case. These are conditions on the result, not doubts about it.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture in the AEC setting; under large-cardinal or weak-GCH hypotheses.

events.what_happened: Espíndola, 'A proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture and an extension to accessible categories with directed colimits', arXiv 1906.09169 (sole author), v1 21 June 2019 under the title 'A topos-theoretic proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for abstract elementary classes', latest v7 13 April 2022. Claims a ZFC proof of Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs; assuming SCH, extends to accessible categories with directed colimits. For theories in L_{κ,θ} under SCH, claims an infinitary Morley-type theorem ('Corollary 9.4: Morley's categoricity theorem for infinitary theories') over a specified class of cardinals, with an example showing the exceptions are necessary. The θ = ω case is described in the text as a generalization of Shelah's original conjecture for sentences in L_{ω1,ω}. The threshold for the L_{κ,θ} case is 'the maximum of the Hanf numbers for categoricity and non-categoricity' (proof of Theorem 9.3), not given as ℶ_{ω1}.
events.revisions: v1 21 Jun 2019 (topos-theoretic title); v2 3 Jul 2019; v3 25 Jul 2019; v4 7 Aug 2019; v5 28 Aug 2019; v6 28 Dec 2020; v7 13 Apr 2022 (current; ZFC for AECs, ZFC+SCH for accessible categories). The v1–v4 abstract assumed GCH and a measurable cardinal (per search-summary text); v7 comment: 'Arguments are now cast in ZFC for abstract elementary classes'.
events.delivers: Claimed: eventual categoricity for AECs in ZFC (not verified). Claimed for L_{κ,θ} under SCH: categoricity transfer over a specified class of cardinals, with exceptions, not a single statement at the bullet's threshold. Whether the θ = ω case gives the bullet's statement (all cardinals above ℶ_{ω1}, sentences in L_{ω1,ω}) is not established on the text read: the threshold is the paper's own Hanf-number maximum, and the exceptions are not characterised in the parts read.
events.remains: Per the paper's own text, the remaining parts are: (a) confirmation that the θ = ω, countable-vocabulary case covers all sentences of L_{ω1,ω}; (b) the threshold equal to the Hanf number of the logic (ℶ_{ω1} in the cited literature), with no exceptional cardinals above it; (c) independent verification, which is not found.

checked_by.qualification: Unclear: an informal forum post by an unnamed participant
checked_by.what_they_did: Informal remark that the work is 'very interesting to the model theory community but is not yet independently checked nor widely accepted' and that some parts are not clear to experts. UNVERIFIED: the page returned HTTP 403 and the text appears only in a search summary; the post is undated and may predate v7.

events.time_since_posted: 7 years since v1 (June 2019); 4.5 years since the latest revision (April 2022); no journal reference on the arXiv listing.
events.doubts: (1) No journal publication or referee report found as of the arXiv listing (v7, April 2022); the arXiv comment field says only that the arguments are cast in ZFC. (2) The v1–v4 version assumed GCH and a measurable cardinal, and the final version drops that; the earlier hypotheses were then removed by a later rewrite, which is a change in scope between versions, recorded here without a verdict. (3) The v7 full text was read in three chunks (characters 0–238,818): no referee, errata, or verification statement; no acknowledgements; no mention of AI, Lean or computer assistance. (4) The nLab forum remark (point above) is the only public engagement found, and it is unverified and undated. (5) The L_{κ,θ} statement is an infinitary Morley-type theorem over a class of cardinals with exceptions, not the bullet's statement. None of these is a finding of error; they are the reasons the claim cannot be taken as established on the public record found.
events.direction: Claims a proof of the eventual categoricity conjecture for AECs (ZFC), and for L_{κ,θ} under SCH a transfer over a class of cardinals with exceptions. Consistent with the bullet's shape; the threshold and exceptions are not stated as the bullet's statement.

events.what_happened: Baldwin, Laskowski and Shelah, 'When does ℵ_1-categoricity imply ω-stability?', arXiv 2308.13942 submitted 26 August 2023; Model Theory 3 (2024) 801–823. For an ℵ_1-categorical atomic class with a model of size ℶ_1^+, the class is ω-stable.
events.revisions: v1 only per the fetched page; journal 2024 (Model Theory).
events.delivers: Atomic ℵ_1-categorical classes: properties of types over the ℵ_1 model and ω-stability from a model of size ℶ_1^+. Restriction: atomic classes, not L_{ω1,ω} sentences; the categoricity cardinal is ℵ_1; the page does not mention L_{ω1,ω} or AECs.
events.remains: The whole bullet. This is a neighbouring categoricity result in a different setting.
events.direction: Neighbouring; no bearing on whether categoricity above the threshold transfers.

events.what_happened: Marangelis, 'Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities', arXiv 2410.19515, submitted 25 October 2024 (math.LO). Builds an L_{ω1,ω} sentence ψ_α coding ℵ_{α+1}-Kurepa trees, with spectrum results. The 'Shelah's conjecture' in this paper is the local Hanf number conjecture: if ℵ_{ω1} < 2^{ℵ_0} and an L_{ω1,ω} sentence has a model of size ℵ_{ω1}, then it has a model of size 2^{ℵ_0}. The paper shows that replacing 2^{ℵ_0} by 2^{ℵ_{α+1}} makes 'no local Hanf number' consistent.
events.revisions: v1 25 Oct 2024 (the arXiv listing shows one version; the PDF header is said to name two other authors).
events.delivers: A consistency result on the spectrum of an L_{ω1,ω} sentence and on the local Hanf number below 2^{ℵ_0}, replaced by 2^{ℵ_{α+1}}. Restriction: a different Shelah conjecture (local Hanf number, not categoricity); it is a namesake, not this bullet.
events.remains: The whole bullet: this paper has no categoricity content.
events.doubts: Authorship is inconsistent between the arXiv listing (one author) and the PDF header, as reported by the fetch. Not relevant to the bullet.
events.direction: Different conjecture sharing a name. Does not change what the bullet's entry should say.

disputes.summary: Boney and Vasey (2015) report a gap in Shelah's proof of a claim about AECs categorical in unboundedly many cardinals, and an earlier version of their own paper contained a mistake. This is a correction within the AEC literature, not a dispute over the L_{ω1,ω} bullet; it is recorded because the claim is one of the inputs to Shelah's approach to the wider conjecture.

The literature gives different thresholds for the same 'Hanf number' wording: ℶ_{ω1} (Shelah 1983 Conjecture 2 as cited by Boney–Vasey 2015, and nLab); i_{ω1} (one search-summary source); ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}} for the universal-sentence theorem (Vasey 2016); ℶ_ω for the universal end-segment theorem (Vasey 2018); and 'max of the Hanf numbers for categoricity and non-categoricity' (Espíndola 2019). Recorded, not reconciled.

summary: Searches (32 WebSearch queries, one in extended mode, plus roughly 20 WebFetch calls on arXiv, journal, Lean, seminar and forum pages, including retries after failed fetches) found no result since 26 January 2024 that settles or moves the L_{ω1,ω} categoricity bullet. The frozen wording (Wikipedia list, local page.wiki line 393) names the L_{ω1,ω} sentence case with 'the Hanf number' and no numerical threshold. The literature's standard form (Shelah 1983 Conjecture 2, as cited by Boney–Vasey 2015 and nLab) takes a countable language and threshold ℶ_{ω1}, and is described as open (Shelah 1990 book, problem D.(3a), per a search summary; not opened). Positive partial results found: Vasey's universal-sentence theorem (Selecta 2017, threshold ℶ_{ℶ_{ω1}}) and end-segment theorem (JSL, threshold ℶ_ω), both restricted to universal sentences; Keisler's 1971 result under sequential homogeneity (unverified, secondary only). The one claim that reaches the L_{ω1,ω} case without restriction to universal sentences is Espíndola's arXiv 1906.09169 (v1 June 2019, latest April 2022, no journal reference found): it claims a ZFC proof of the AEC eventual categoricity conjecture, and for L_{κ,θ} under SCH a transfer over a specified class of cardinals with exceptions, with threshold the paper's own Hanf-number maximum. Its full text (read in three chunks) contains no referee statement, acknowledgements, or AI/Lean/computer mention. Close call 1: whether Espíndola's θ = ω case (Corollary 9.4) is the bullet's statement. The paper calls it a generalization of Shelah's original conjecture, but it gives no threshold equal to ℶ_{ω1} and characterises exceptions it does not spell out in the parts read, so the reading that it settles the bullet is not established here. Close call 2: whether 'categorical above the Hanf number' means in some or in all cardinals above it; the standard reading is 'some', recorded here. Close call 3: whether Shelah–Vasey JEMS 2024 is 'in window': the journal year is 2024, but the first written argument is the 2018 preprint, so the event is dated 2018 per §5.1. AI search: no AI system is named in any source read for this bullet; none_found is true throughout. The only AI-related items found were outside this bullet: arXiv 2609.00436 (Freitag and Mutchnik, 31 August 2026, 'A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture', credited to 'ChatGPT 5.6' for constructing the counterexample; the authors say proofs were 'written entirely by the authors'); it is a different problem and is not an event here. The Lean evaluation page for Morley's categoricity theorem is a first-order countable-language stub containing sorry, not the L_{ω1,ω} case. Not an event: Marangelis 2024 ('Shelah's conjecture fails for higher cardinalities') is a namesake about the local Hanf number below 2^ℵ0; it is recorded as an event with that reason. Discarded neighbours recorded: Baldwin–Laskowski–Shelah 2023 (atomic ℵ_1-categoricity), Kolman–Shelah 1996 and Makkai–Shelah 1990 (different logics, large-cardinal hypotheses), Sh:394 (AEC amalgamation).
competing_reading: Espíndola's 2019 arXiv 1906.09169 may settle the bullet: its θ = ω case is labelled a generalization of Shelah's original conjecture, and its threshold is 'the Hanf number for categoricity and non-categoricity', which for L_{ω1,ω} could be ℶ_{ω1}. On that reading the bullet is resolved as of v7 (April 2022) by an unrefereed ZFC proof, with the earlier GCH and measurable-cardinal versions superseded. The case against: no journal acceptance or verification was found; the paper's own statement is a transfer over a class of cardinals with exceptions; and the threshold is not stated as ℶ_{ω1}. A reader who takes 'categorical above the Hanf number' to mean 'in all cardinals above' would find the bullet trivial, which argues against that reading. The standard 'some cardinal above' reading is what the sources use.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The statement of Theorem 9.1 and Corollary 9.4 in 1906.09169, with the value of the Hanf number χ for L_{ω1,ω} and whether the exceptional class of cardinals is empty above ℶ_{ω1}. (2) A journal publication or a published referee report or verification of 1906.09169. (3) A primary source for Shelah's 1983 Conjecture 2 and the 1990 book's problem D.(3a), giving the threshold and the statement exactly. (4) Opened primary sources for Keisler 1971 and Makkai–Shelah 1990, which were only seen in summaries. (5) The nForum thread 3902 page, which returned 403 here.
